column1: # Test cases for ambashador, one per line, in the form:
# hook should fall through to the interactive prompt) or 'explain' (fall through
# and additionally return a 'context' string advising the model). Blank lines and
# lines beginning with '#' are ignored. Leading and trailing whitespace in the
# command is significant and preserved, so cases can cover odd spacing.
# Commands that are simply not on the allowlist.
# 'find' is allowed for search, but execution and deletion flags are denied.
# 'git' is allowed only for read-only subcommands, named immediately after it.

column2: git ls-files '*AGENTS*' '*CRUSH*'; test -d node_modules && printf 'node_modules exists'
column3: git -c core.fsmonitor=false ls-files -- '*AGENTS*' '*CRUSH*'; test -d node_modules && printf 'node_modules exists'

column1: # Pipelines: the first stage uses the full allowlist, later stages the narrower
# 'tee' is a deliberate file-writing exception, allowed in either position.
# 'sed' must be explicitly sandboxed wherever it appears. An un-sandboxed sed is
# rejected with advice rather than a bare fall-through.
# 'man' allows safe reading of manual pages, but arbitrary pagers/browsers/local files are denied.
# 'nm' allows inspecting symbol tables, but external plugins or response files are denied.
# 'objdump' allows disassembling and header dumping, but external commands/plugins/response files are denied.
# File descriptor duplication is permitted, but only in the '<digit>>&<digit>'
# form and only where it cannot mask a real redirect or a backgrounding '&'.
# File redirection and discarding output are permitted after a command.
# Shell redirection to a file is allowed; redirection to a command is denied.
# 'rg' allows searching, but preprocessors ('--pre') are denied.
# Substitution, escapes and backgrounding are always rejected.
# Escapes in double quotes are unescaped safely; unescaped substitutions are rejected.
# Compound commands, subshells and control structures are rejected.

column2: for f in *; do ls; done
